### 1. The skill-score equation appears to have the wrong sign

The paper defines

\[
\text{skill} = \frac{C_{\text{base}} - C_{\text{agent}}}{C_{\text{orc}} - C_{\text{base}}}.
\]

But lower cost is better, and the oracle is generally cheaper than the base-stock floor, so \(C_{\text{orc}} < C_{\text{base}}\). This denominator is therefore negative. ...

The paper reports:

\[
(9101 - 8539)/(9101 - 6932) = 0.26.
\]

That corresponds to

\[
\frac{C_{\text{base}} - C_{\text{agent}}}{C_{\text{base}} - C_{\text{orc}}},
\]

not the equation printed in the paper.

This is not merely typographical: it affects the interpretation of negative headroom, values above 1, and all reported skill scores. The authors should correct the formula and ensure that every table and statement is consistent with the corrected definition.
